cards.text: Here in Isaiah, the LORD speaks, and He opens with a short to-do list: 'Maintain justice and do what is right.' Two items, baker. TWO. I've lost longer lists than that under the takeout menus in my old junk drawer.

cards.question: Do what's right, the LORD says, because His ___ is coming soon.

cards.text: His righteousness will be revealed too. And the man who holds it fast? The LORD calls him blessed. Not 'pretty good.' Not 'nice try.' BLESSED.

cards.question: The blessed man keeps his hand from doing any evil. What else does he keep without profaning it?

cards.text: Then the passage turns to two people who I bet are feeling left out. First up, a foreigner who has joined himself to the LORD.

cards.question: What should the foreigner who has joined himself to the LORD not say?

answers.text: The LORD will shut me out of His people
The LORD will take away all of my land
The LORD will send me back to my country

cards.text: Next, the eunuch shouldn't say, 'I am but a dry tree.' Friend, after years in a junk drawer, I was a dry tree with a MUSTACHE.
Then the LORD Himself answers. He speaks to the eunuchs who keep His Sabbaths, choose what pleases Him and hold fast to His covenant.

cards.question: In His house and within His walls, what does the LORD give those eunuchs?

answers.text: A name better than sons and daughters
A place among the priests of Israel
A share of land for their families

cards.question: The name the LORD gives these eunuchs will last only as long as they live.

cards.text: An everlasting name that will not be cut off. The Millers carved 'Dorin' into my handle, and I STILL ended up behind the takeout menus in the junk drawer.
Now back to the foreigners. The LORD speaks of the ones who join themselves to Him to minister to Him, to love His name and to be His servants.

cards.question: These foreigners also keep the Sabbath and hold fast to the LORD's covenant.
Where does the LORD say He'll bring those foreigners?
Once they're on His holy mountain, the LORD says He'll make the foreigners ___ in His house of prayer.
At the LORD's altar, the foreigners' burnt offerings and sacrifices will be turned away.
The LORD accepts their offerings, for His house will be called a house of prayer for whom?

cards.text: Then the Lord GOD, who gathers the dispersed of Israel, has one last word. Meanwhile, I've been chasing the same three sprinkles across my bakery floor since Tuesday.

cards.question: The Lord GOD says He's done gathering once Israel's scattered people are brought in.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: the setup with the quote, 'Two items, baker.', 'TWO.' and the junk drawer line. That is over the 3-sentence limit.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the wording of the line. Nothing on card 1 lets the baker reason that it's 'salvation' rather than 'judgment' or 'kingdom'. 'Do what's right because judgment is coming soon' makes just as much sense, so the pick comes down to luck.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This story card has 6 sentences and fragments: 'His righteousness will be revealed too.', 'And the man who holds it fast?', 'The LORD calls him blessed.', 'Not 'pretty good.'', 'Not 'nice try.'' and 'BLESSED.' The limit is 1 to 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The setup says the foreigner and the eunuch are 'feeling left out'. That gives away card 6's right answer, 'The LORD will shut me out of His people', and rules out the land and send-back answers.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This card restates 'An everlasting name that will not be cut off', which card 10 already established. It doesn't move the passage forward. It is a recap that carries a joke.
Both wrong answers start with 'Only' ('Only the priests' and 'Only the twelve tribes'). That makes 'All the nations' the one answer that sounds different, so it stands out as the right answer.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
